REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
AND SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
THURSDAY - DECEMBER 8, 2022 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. 6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Joo Pak, representing 67th District Assemblymember Sharon Quirk-Silva, introduced
  himself to the Council, staff, and community.

  Renita Armstrong, Bellflower Unified School District Governing Boardmember, introduced
  herself to the Council, staff, and community.

  Norma Williamson commented on the impacts to residents from heatwaves and
  blackouts, and suggested the City Council install a solar/battery cooling system at the
  Cerritos Senior Center. She submitted documents for the record entitled, "Facing a
  sizzling summer, large parts of the U.S. risk blackouts, government agency warns,” and
  a community petition entitled, “Cerritos Community Petition to install a solar/battery
  storage cooling system on Cerritos Senior Center.”

  Suzanne Philipsen-Zabel expressed her care for Cerritos community and suggested the
  City Council install a solar/battery cooling system at the Cerritos Senior Center.

  Al Barlevy suggested the City Council install a solar/battery cooling system at the
  Cerritos Senior Center and other City facilities and cited the City’s support of the
  generation of clean energy through the original Magnolia Power Plant project.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

9C.  Review and consideration of announcement of City Manager Art Gallucci’s retirement
  from the City of Cerritos and consideration of process for recruitment of a new City
  Manager (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Bill Ihrke, City Attorney. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  City Council discussion ensued on the agenda item.

  MOTION FAILS DUE TO LACK OF A SECOND: The motion made by Johnson to reorder
  the agenda for the purpose of adjourning to Closed Session at this juncture of the meeting
  for the purpose of discussing Closed Session Item 12A (City Manager Performance
  Evaluation) did not pass due to lack of a second.

  The City Council resumed discussion on this agenda item.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Anantha Ramachandran thanked City Manager Gallucci on his years of service to the
  City of Cerritos and suggested the City Council use this opportunity to consider Charter
  amendments as related to the City Manager position, including salary caps and term
  limits.

  Rosa Peters expressed concerns that the process for the selection of a new City Manager
  appears to lack transparency.

  Gabriela Dominguez expressed the need for transparency in the selection of a new City
  Manager and suggested the matter be tabled until additional information is presented
  regarding each option.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record. Full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Gail and Marty Grossman provided suggestions for selection of the next City Manager.

  Sue Carter expressed gratitude for City Manager Gallucci’s years of service to the City of
  Cerritos and provided suggestions for the selection of the next City Manager.

  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MAIN MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Barrows, to direct staff to
  provide an agenda report to the City Council with information and costs related to retaining a
  professional recruiting service for the purpose of selection of a new City Manager (COUNCIL).

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Yokoyama, to table
  consideration of this matter until such time as City staff can provide an agenda report with
  information in response to the various inquiries and requests made by the City Council
  during their discussion, as summarized below:

  -  Comprehensive options available to the City Council as related to the selection of a
  new City Manager, inclusive of specific detail, timelines, and associated costs; List to
  include all items presented during City Attorney’s staff report and PowerPoint
  Presentation, survey of recent City Manager selection processes conducted by local,
  regional, and statewide municipalities, and other recommended best practices;

  -  Legal parameters and specificity as to which topics and matters can be discussed or
  disclosed in open session versus closed session as related to the City Manager position,
  including specific cash payout amounts upon retirement;

  -  Detailed information, specific dollar amounts, and financial impacts related to
  employment and separation agreements (if any), compensation, benefits, vacation,
  sick time and cash payout policies, retirement benefits and provisions, CalPERS
  policies, PARS policies, City policies, and any other related financial matters related to
  the current City Manager’s employment and pending retirement from the City of
  Cerritos, inclusive of timelines and specific payout amounts;

  -  City policies as related to the priority given to internal City candidates versus external
  candidates for promotional opportunities;

  -  Detailed information related to the financial impacts to the City and current City
  Manager of any Citywide salary increases awarded prior to his June 30, 2023
  retirement;

  -  Information on “caps” on vacation, sick leave, benefits, and other financial matters, as
  related to the City Manager position;

  -  Detailed information on Cerritos City Charter sections, which apply to the City Manager
  position;

  -  Policies for use of accrued vacation and sick time by the current City Manager; and

  -  Information on internal transition plan, should the current City Manager elect to use
  longer term (two weeks or more) accrued vacation and/or sick time, prior to his
  projected June 30, 2023 retirement date (COUNCIL).
